MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 23, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on August 23, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 18, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel Pursuant to Government Code 54957(a) on Matters
  Posing a Threat to Public Services, Facilities and Operations

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel- Anticipated Litigation Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: Two
  anticipated cases; one adverse to Mayor Ury and the other adverse to the City,
  both as threatened by Capistrano Unified School District ("CUSD") after it held
City Council Minutes  1  August 23, 2016
   closed session(s) and announced its decision in public. The apparent reason for the
  threats of lawsuit against a public official and the City is as regards the City and its
  official(s) expressing concerns and issues in relation to a proposed but not yet adopted
  public finance bond measure proposed by CUSD

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for item CS1, the Council considered and discussed
matters posing a threat to public services, facilities and operations. The City will be providing an
interim response to the Grand Jury and continue research related to the Grand Jury's position on
drones and drone operation. Mr. Curley noted that item CS2 had to do with the Capistrano Unified
School District (CUSD) Board of Trustees’ displeasure with the City of Mission Viejo and the
City of Rancho Santa Margarita, and their elected officials, providing feedback and expressing
concerns during the public input stage of the CUSD bond discussion. The CUSD Board recently
announced that they are going to sue both cities and both Mayors. Tonight, the Mission Viejo City
Council authorized the City Attorney’s office to commence preparation of the defense of the City.
The Council has presently not acted on the defense of the Mayor and if there is individual litigation
brought against Mayor Ury, he will be defending himself on his own budget.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

PUBLIC COMMENTS

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 15, and 20 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

  professional services for the Pavement Management Program. She asked why a consultant
City Council Minutes  4  August 23, 2016
   needs to look at the pavement report that was conducted by Nichols Consulting Engineers

6.  Check Register Dated July 29, 2016 in the Amount of $684,499.39

  Council Member Schlicht reminded her colleagues that she is interested in playground
  equipment for pre-teens and asked for a status of the Community Services Commission's
  review.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay said that he doesn't
  remember the Council taking action to direct the Community Services Commission to
  determine what sites might be appropriate for middle school-aged children. He
  recommended asking the Commission to develop criteria for amenities for pre-teens as a

13.  Project V Local Transit Cooperative Agreement

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented staff report and answered the City

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the study was conducted in 2008 before

  with the private marketplace.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed the addition of a stop at Capistrano Valley High
  School and asked that the City's branding be included on the buses.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1)
  approve Cooperative Agreement No. C-6-1292 between the Orange County Transportation

  Transit/Circulators; and (2) adopted Resolution 16-41 Establishing Fund 222 for Project
  V Grant Fund, Program 525 for Project V Community-Based Transit/Circulator Operations
  and CIP 234 for Associated Capital Costs and Amending the FY 2016-17 Budget for Costs
  Related to Fund 222, Program 525 and CIP 234.

City Council Minutes  6  August 23, 2016

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to

PUBLIC HEARINGS

22.  Proposed Abatement of Weeds on Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed
  Abatement Program 2016 - Phase 2.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the report.

  At the hour of 6:31 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing.

  Esther Tsai, M.V.: expressed her objection to the City's proposal to remove weeds on her
  property. She stated that the plants in her yard serve as a slope stabilizer and she weeds
  the yard monthly.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay pointed out that Mrs.
  Tsai's property is on the list of property owners that have recently come into compliance
  with the City's request to remove weeds.

  Mayor Ury closed the public hearing at 6:36 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to instruct
  the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in
  accordance with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Update on CUSD Bond Measure

  Mayor Ury noted that Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD) had been invited to come
  to prior Council Meetings and was scheduled to make a presentation this evening. City
  Manager Wilberg shared that last week, Superintendent Vitale told her that the CUSD
  Board had directed her to not attend the Council meeting tonight as a result of the fact that
  the City Council has already taken a position against the measure. Director of
  Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas outlined her attendance at the CUSD Board Meeting
  on August 10, 2016, and noted that the Board Members came out of closed session and
  announced that they would initiate litigation against the City of Mission Viejo and Mayor
  Ury and the City of Rancho Santa Margarita and its Mayor. At that meeting, the CUSD
  Board also approved the placement of the bond measure on the November 8, 2016, ballot
  with a vote of 6-1 with Trustee Reardon voting no.

City Council Minutes  9  August 23, 2016
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg distributed a copy of the recently completed Community Opinion Survey
and announced that True North Research will provide a detailed presentation on the survey at the
next City Council meeting and also at the September 8 Vision Plan workshop.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths asked about the road construction at Marguerite Parkway and College
Drive. City Manager Wilberg responded that the work is being done by Moulton Niguel Water
District and is somewhat related to the burst pipe that was reported earlier. Council Member Raths
announced that he enjoys attending ribbon cutting ceremonies and meeting new business owners
in town. He recently stopped at the Kaleidoscope shopping center where the escalators are
working and the new Union Market has opened for business. Council Member Raths encouraged
residents to stop by Kaleidoscope and check it out.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs let residents know that AB1217 did pass the Assembly and is on the way
to the Governor's desk. He stated that the proposed legislation is a real intrusion into local
operations and will take local control away regarding the Joint Powers Authority. Council
Member Sachs drew attention to the results of the recent community opinion survey. He said the
results were amazing and the consultant was looking for about 400 respondents but got 798
respondents, leaving just a 3.5% margin of error. Council Member Sachs announced that the
consultant, True North, will be at the next meeting to make a presentation and in the meantime, he
highlighted that 74% of respondents supported the City playing an active role in the revitalization
process which is an increase of over 9% since the 2008 survey. 63% said the shopping center in
the core area of town is in need of revitalization, 68% said there is too little entertainment, 78% of
the community believes that improvements will help attract businesses and jobs and 76% feel that
it will improve the local economy and help generate more revenue. He noted that one of the most
important takeaways had to do with high-density housing and 92.8% of Mission Viejo residents
feel the city has enough or too much housing already. Council Member Sachs added that he has
personally told two developers, over the last ten days, that the City is not interested in more
development.

City Council Minutes  10  August 23, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

30.  A report to the Citizens of Mission Viejo on the Kosmont Report: The Retail and
  Market Strategy with potential for infilling commercial properties with mixed-use
  development including residential

  The City Council received and filed Council Member Schlicht’s report.

Council Member Schlicht stated that Cox is losing viewership and increasing its fees and she asked
staff if Cox franchise fees are going up or down. She noted that she was the lone no vote on the
annexation of property for the Standard Pacific housing project at the north end of town. The
houses are now selling for $1.2 million and HOA fees are around $350. She asked if that includes
street light and street maintenance. Council Member Schlicht drew attention to the black American
flag that she was displaying on the dais which was designed to support peace officers and first
responders. The courage exhibited by officers in the line of duty is represented by the thin blue
line in the center of the flag and the solemn black background acts as a memorial to the lives lost
while shielding citizens from anarchy. In closing, Council Member Schlicht shared a quote from
George Washington, "The power under the constitution will always be in the people. It is entrusted
for certain defined purposes, and for a certain limited period, to representatives of their own
choosing.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum commented on Council Member Schlicht's agenda report for item
30. She stated that Council Member Schlicht was aware of the scope of the $30,000 Kosmont
report and the scope of the second agreement with Kosmont which she approved with a yes
vote. She noted that Council Member Schlicht approved 100% of the funding for economic
development which to date equals $620,000 for both the 15-16 and 16-17 fiscal years. She also
stated that when Council Member Schlicht approved the $300,000 fudging in October 2015 she
knew it was the intent of the City to hire a consultant which was the SWA contract. Council
Member Schlicht made no objections during the votes leading up to the Kosmont contract and
didn’t vote no until the contract was presented. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reminded residents of
the Mission for the Armed Forces and Honor Bowl football games at Mission Viejo High School
on Labor Day weekend. Also, on August 25, the Nadadores will hold an event to raise money for
the aquatics center improvements and she encouraged the community to stop by. Mayor Pro Tem
Bucknum announced that the Orange County Association of Realtors will hold the South Orange
County Economic Coalition and will be discussing the CUSD bond measure on Friday, August
26. Mayor Ury will offer one perspective and CUSD Superintendent Vitale will offer another
perspective at that meeting. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum deferred to Council Member Sachs who
announced that the next Vision Plan workshop will be held on Thursday, September 8 at 6:30 p.m.
in the Saddleback Room at city hall. In closing, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated Islands
Restaurant on their move from Kaleidoscope over to the Shops at Mission Viejo and she
encouraged millennial residents to visit the Union Market restaurants where they will find a cool,
hip vibe.

City Council Minutes  11  August 23, 2016
 Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury wished everyone a nice Labor Day weekend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:23 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 13, at 5:00 p.m.
